issues.issue: The precedence rule says the Agreement prevails over an inconsistent Confirmation 'unless each party has executed such Confirmation', leaving it unclear which document governs when only one party signs or when the Confirmation is made through a comparison system under 2.1(b).

Section 2.1 makes the Agreement prevail over inconsistent Confirmations, while Schedule B section 2 makes the Schedule prevail over the Agreement, leaving a three-document hierarchy that is nowhere fully ordered.
The sentence is broken mid-clause ('regarding when a Loan unless otherwise agreed'), so the condition it purports to override cannot be identified from the words used.

Section 2.2 says no Loan occurs until both Loaned Securities and Collateral have been transferred, while Section 4.1 expressly contemplates Collateral being transferred after the securities (up to Close of Business that day) and Section 4.4 addresses one-sided transfers.

The recharacterisation trigger, 'if any Loan is deemed to be a loan of money', does not say by whom or on what standard the deeming occurs, so the condition on which the security interest arises is undefined.
The required amount is the 'Margin Percentage' of Market Value, and that percentage is defined twice with different content in Section 25.37 and Schedule B section 6.

'Lender may use or invest the Collateral, if such consists of cash, at its own risk' is open to two readings: that the Lender bears investment losses on cash collateral, or merely that it acts without the Borrower's warranty while the loss allocation lies elsewhere. The same sentence's segregation duty ('unless Lender is a Broker-Dealer') sits awkwardly with a permission to invest.
'Absolute right to the return' is not tied to any procedure or time limit, and it is unclear how it interacts with the Section 13 remedies for the same failure to transfer.
The proviso setting out what substituted Collateral must consist of breaks off after '(a) consist only of cash,', so the conditions on substitution cannot be applied as written.

The carve-out reads 'Except as set forth in Sections 3.1 and 8.2', but Section 3.1 concerns Lender's transfer of securities and contains no exception to Borrower's incidents of ownership; the intended reference is evidently Section 8.1.
The final obligation is cut off ('Borrower shall forthwith transfer the ...'), so what must be transferred on a terminated Loan is not stated.

The conditional structure is broken: clause (a) reads 'transfer of cash cash or other property by Lender would give rise to a Margin Deficit' and the counterpart limb (Borrower/Margin Excess) is missing, so the trigger for crediting instead of transferring cannot be applied.

Section 9.1 fixes a flat 100% collateral level for Customer loans, while Sections 9.2/25.37 and Schedule B section 6 set the requirement by reference to a 'Margin Percentage' that may be higher, and the two mark-to-market regimes are not expressly reconciled.
The demand right runs on the 'Margin Percentage', which Section 25.37 and Schedule B section 6 define differently, so the level triggering a Margin Deficit depends on which definition controls.

The representation is qualified by compliance with 'Section 11.1(b)', which requires execution of 'Annex I', but the annex made applicable by Schedule B section 1 is Annex I-A, so the condition points to a document not incorporated by that name.
The waiver refers to 'the representation or warranty in subsection (6)', a mis-citation of subsection (a), so the representation being disapplied is identified only by inference.

Section 11.1(b) requires execution of and compliance with 'Annex I', but Schedule B section 1 makes 'Annex I-A (Agency Annex)' the applicable annex, leaving the agency election tied to a differently named document.

The remedy turns on purchasing replacement securities and selling Collateral 'in a commercially reasonable manner', an unmeasured standard that also governs the damages computation against the Borrower.

Borrower's remedy likewise depends on the undefined 'commercially reasonable manner' standard, and on a deemed-price election 'in its sole discretion' from 'a generally recognized source', with no criterion for choosing that source.

Where no generally recognised price source exists the non-defaulting party may fix the source 'in its sole discretion', with no standard limiting that choice even though it sets the measure of damages.

The clause defines 'securities' to include 'security entitlements' 'as used herein (except in this Section 15)', an exclusion that is hard to square with the same Section's rules on transferring 'financial assets' and obtaining 'control'.

The ERISA regime is triggered only if Lender notifies Borrower that Plan assets are involved, and the section does not say what happens to a Loan in fact funded with Plan assets where no notice was given.

The consequence of Lender's failure to 'communicate and keep current' the fiduciary information is that Lender 'shall be deemed to have made' Borrower's representation, a deeming whose scope and effect on the Loan is not spelled out.
The daily mark-to-market duty is imposed 'pursuant to Section 9.7', but the Agreement's Section 9 ends at 9.6, so the operative mechanic is cited to a provision that does not exist.

Delivery is due within 'the lesser of' three periods including 'the time negotiated for such delivery', yet the proviso allows the parties to agree a longer period, so a negotiated longer period is both included in and excluded from the 'lesser of' test.

This makes Collateral security 'only' for Borrower's obligations to the Plan, whereas Section 4.2 makes Collateral security for 'any other obligations of Borrower to Lender hereunder' and Section 18 allows set-off across all Loans.

The single-agreement, cross-default and cross-Loan set-off treatment is difficult to reconcile with Annex I-A section 4, which treats the portion of each Loan allocable to each Principal as a separate Loan, and with Section 17.4(d)'s Plan-only collateral limit.

Section 21 makes all obligations with respect to any Loan survive termination of the Agreement, while Section 24.1 permits termination on notice 'subject only to fulfillment of any obligations then outstanding', leaving the post-termination position stated two different ways.

A notice is 'deemed effective' when 'delivery was in good faith attempted' even if never received, and 'good faith attempted' is given no content; the telephone proviso adds a further undefined precondition.

The integration clause is opened by 'Except as otherwise agreed by the parties' and is limited to agreements 'concerning loans of Securities', so which prior or collateral arrangements survive is left genuinely open.

Termination on notice is 'subject only to fulfillment of any obligations then outstanding', which does not say whether termination is deferred until outstanding Loans are closed or is immediate with obligations surviving.

The no-oral-modification rule cannot easily be squared with Section 24.2, which expressly allows agreements under Sections 10.5(b) and 25.37 to be made orally, and with the definitions of Close of Business and Cutoff Time that permit agreement 'orally or in writing'.
'Time is of the essence' sits uneasily with Sections 12.4 and 12.8, which make a failure a Default only after notice and a cure period running to the next day's Cutoff Time.
Section 24.2 permits agreements to be made orally if promptly confirmed, which pulls against the same Section 24.1 requirement that the Agreement be modified only by a signed writing.

The definition ends its enumerated insolvency laws with the catch-all 'or similar law', leaving the reach of that phrase (for example to regulatory or receivership regimes) to be fixed by construction.

The definition sweeps in any such person 'regardless of whether the activities of such person are conducted in the United States or otherwise require such person to register', which makes the class broader than the enumerated registered categories suggest and controls Lender's Retransfer and segregation duties under Section 4.2.

'Business Day' is given three different meanings in one definition (by reference to the Loaned Securities' market, to the market of the security being valued, and a special Section 9 meaning), so which applies to any given deadline is not always plain.
The definition cross-refers to 'Section 3.1', but 'Cash Collateral Fee' is defined in Section 5.1; Section 3.1 concerns transfer of Loaned Securities and contains no such definition.

Failing agreement, 'Close of Business' is whatever is 'determined in accordance with market practice', an unspecified external standard that fixes the deadline for collateral and payment obligations throughout the Agreement.

The definition's residual limb for a Customer Lender extends to 'any other property permitted to serve as collateral ... pursuant to exemptive, interpretive or no-action relief or otherwise', a catch-all whose boundary against the enumerated cash, Treasuries and letters of credit is indeterminate.

Whether a Lender is a 'Customer' turns on being a customer of Borrower 'under Rule 15c3-3 ... (to the extent that Borrower is subject to such Rule)', and that status switches on Sections 9.1, 4.2 and the Collateral definition without any test the parties can apply on their own.
Absent agreement the 'Cutoff Time' is left to 'market practice', an undefined external benchmark although it governs when transfers under Sections 3, 4, 6 and 12 become late.

'Distribution' is defined by an open list headed 'including, but not limited to', beginning with the wholly general 'cash and all other property', so the reach of the enumerated categories against that general limb is uncertain.

Securities count as 'Foreign Securities' if 'principally cleared and settled outside the United States', and 'principally' is given no measure although the label switches the default interest rate under Sections 13.1 and 13.2.
The definition breaks off mid-sentence at 'if at least two such rates appear, the arithmetic mean of', so the fallback rate-setting mechanic is incomplete as written.
The definition omits the section number entirely ('shall have the meaning assigned in Section'), leaving the cross-reference blank.

Absent agreement the Margin Notice Deadline is 'the deadline for such purposes established in accordance with market practice', an unfixed external standard that determines whether margin must be met the same day or the next.

The floor is 100% 'unless (a) Borrower and Lender agree otherwise ... and (b) Lender is not a Customer', so it is unclear whether both conditions must be satisfied to displace the floor and what percentage applies if only one is.
Schedule B section 6 purports to restate 'Margin Percentage' with different figures, so the operative percentage depends on reconciling this definition with that Schedule provision.

Where Annex II or another writing does not apply, Market Value is set 'in accordance with market practice' from 'a generally recognized source agreed to by the parties', leaving the valuation of collateral and loaned securities to an unfixed standard.

The definition says its determinations apply 'for all purposes under this Agreement, except for purposes of Section 13', yet Section 13 itself measures damages by Market Value concepts and prices from 'a generally recognized source', so the carve-out leaves the default valuation rule unstated.
'Retransfer' is defined by a list of specific dealings closing with the general 'or otherwise transfer such Collateral', leaving the catch-all's reach against the enumerated acts open.

'Securities' is defined circularly as 'securities or, if agreed by the parties in writing, other assets', which supplies no boundary and lets the central subject matter of the Agreement be anything the parties write down.

The characterisation is qualified by 'except insofar as the type of assets subject to the Loan would render such definition inapplicable', a self-cancelling proviso that leaves the status of any given Loan to be decided later.

The disclosure tells Lender that the Collateral delivered may be its only source of satisfaction if Borrower fails to return the Loaned Securities, which pulls against Section 13.1, under which Borrower remains personally liable for any excess and grants Lender a security interest in its other property.

Agent must supply 'such information in its possession necessary to complete all required fields in the format generally used in the industry' and use 'best efforts' as to optional information, warranting accuracy only 'to the best of its knowledge' and excepting 'pseudo tax identification numbers' — a cluster of unfixed standards.

The provision limits Agent's liability and provides that Agent is not to be treated or liable as principal, but its wording is so degraded that the scope of the limitation — which representations it covers and which obligations survive — cannot be fixed from the text.

The limitation of Agent's liability pulls against Section 11.1(a), under which each party agrees either to be liable as principal or to comply with the agency Annex, and against Agent's own continuing representations in Annex I-A section 1.

Treating each Principal's allocable portion as a separate Loan, with obligations determined Principal by Principal, is hard to reconcile with Section 18, which makes all Loans a single relationship with cross-default and cross-Loan set-off.

The clause substitutes 'Principal' for 'Lender' and 'other party' throughout the Agreement, but the text is so degraded that which references are converted, and which rights remain with Agent, cannot be determined from the words.

The listed-securities valuation rule (last sale price, consolidated tape, preceding Close of Trading) is rendered in text so garbled that the operative pricing sequence cannot be read off the provision.

The rule for securities not listed on an exchange rests on 'market practice' and a 'generally recognized source' agreed by the parties, and as written the text is too corrupted to identify the applicable quotation.

Annex II states that its Market Value determinations apply for all purposes of the Agreement 'except for purposes of Section 13', which leaves the valuation standard for the very remedies in Section 13 to be supplied from elsewhere.

The Annex applies to Equity Securities only if a Loan is designated a Term Loan, but makes 'All Loans of Securities other than Equity Securities' Term Loans by default 'unless otherwise agreed', an asymmetric default whose reach over ordinary open loans is not obvious.

The parties must 'use their best efforts to negotiate in good faith' a Replacement Loan of 'comparable or other Securities' 'mutually agreed upon' — an agreement to agree whose breach cannot be measured against any stated criterion.

Imposing a Breakage Fee on 'the party requesting termination' sits against Section 6.1, which lets either party terminate a Loan on notice without charge, and against Annex III section 2, which preserves the Agreement's termination rights for Term Loans.

The Breakage Fee formula — the components of the 'sum of' and how loss on the replacement transaction is measured — is unreadable as written, so the amount payable cannot be computed from the provision.
The list of incorporated annexes names 'Annex I-A (Agency Annex)', whereas Section 11.1(b) and Section 10.3 condition agency status on executing and complying with 'Annex I'.

Schedule B gives itself priority over the Agreement, while Section 2.1 gives the Agreement priority over an unexecuted Confirmation, so the relative rank of Schedule, Agreement and Confirmation is never completely ordered.

The clause binds the parties to 'any uniform practices applicable to securities loans' among members of two named associations, 'as currently in effect, or successor provisions thereto', and only 'to the extent that such market practice ... does not conflict with the terms of the Agreement' — an open-ended incorporation with an undefined conflict test.

The no-reliance representation is preserved only in fragments ('not relying on any communication ... as investment advice or ... except as expressly set forth in the Agreement'), so the scope of what each party disclaims reliance on cannot be fixed from the text.

The independent-judgment representation survives only as a fragment referring to 'its own decisions regarding' the transactions 'based upon its own judgment and upon advice from such advisers as it deemed necessary', leaving what was represented indeterminate.
The representation that each party 'understands the terms, conditions and risks of each Loan' and is 'willing and able to assume' them is both a vague standard and, as reproduced, incomplete.

Schedule B section 6 rewrites 'Margin Percentage' (with different percentages for different securities) in terms that cannot be squared with the not-less-than-100% definition in Section 25.37, leaving the collateral level to depend on which text governs.
